Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of CBD vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which CBD may alter cancer related pathways.

Introduction/Context  
A differential expression (DE) analysis was performed comparing cannabidiol (CBD)-treated versus DMSO-treated colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines. The supplied DEG file (“ijms-24-14743-v2_crc_cells_cbd_vs_dmso_DEG.csv”) contains Ensembl-identified genes with log2-fold changes, p-values, and adjusted p-values (padj). The number of replicates, cell-line names, exact padj cutoff, and total significant gene count are not specified.

Keywords  
• CBD (cannabidiol)  
• Colorectal cancer  
• Reactome pathway  
• Apoptosis  
• Cell cycle  

Candidate Genes  
BAX, CASP3, CCND1, CDK2, BRCA1  

Pathway Over-Representation Analysis (Reactome)  
Statistically significant genes (padj < 0.05) were tested against Reactome gene sets (Reactome_Pathways_2024) using an over-representation analysis (ORA). Top enriched pathways and their overlapping DE genes are summarized below.

| Reactome Pathway             | Overlap Genes                         | Regulation Direction¹             |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Apoptosis                    | BAX (up), CASP3 (up), BCL2 (down)     | Mixed (pro-apoptotic skew)        |
| Cell Cycle, Mitotic          | CCND1 (down), CDK2 (down), E2F1 (down)| Down                               |
| DNA Repair                   | BRCA1 (down), RAD51 (down), ATM (down)| Down                               |
| Signal Transduction          | MAPK1 (down), JUN (up), FOS (up)      | Mixed                              |
| Immune System                | NFKB1 (down), STAT3 (down), IL6 (up)  | Mixed                              |

¹ “up” or “down” denotes the sign of log2FoldChange in the DE results.  
*Note: exact p-values and FDRs for each pathway are not specified in the tool output.*

Balanced Analysis  
• Apoptosis emerged as the top‐enriched pathway, driven by up-regulation of BAX and CASP3 and concurrent down-regulation of the anti-apoptotic BCL2. This suggests CBD shifts the intrinsic apoptosis balance toward cell death.  
• Cell-cycle pathways (especially G1/S and mitotic checkpoints) are significantly enriched for down-regulated drivers (CCND1, CDK2, E2F1), indicating CBD may enforce a G1/S arrest in CRC cells.  
• DNA-repair terms are enriched for down-regulated factors (BRCA1, RAD51, ATM), implying a potential reduction in repair capacity and genomic stability under CBD.  
• Signal transduction modules show a mixed response: pro-proliferative MAPK1 is down, whereas immediate-early transcription factors JUN and FOS are modestly up, indicating a complex rewiring of stress- and mitogen-activated kinase signaling.  
• Immune-related signaling (e.g., NFKB1, STAT3) shows down-regulation, with IL6 up-regulated, hinting that CBD may modulate inflammatory crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment.

Targeted/Keyword-Guided Subset  
Filtering the Reactome ORA for pathways containing “apoptosis,” “cell cycle,” or “signal” confirms these as the most prominently affected modules by CBD (no additional keyword-matching pathways outside those listed above).

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Up-regulated pro-apoptotic genes

| Gene  | Direction | Role/Function           | Pathway(s)      |
|-------|-----------|-------------------------|-----------------|
| BAX   | up        | Pro-apoptotic BCL2 family | Apoptosis      |
| CASP3 | up        | Effector caspase         | Apoptosis      |

Down-regulated cell-cycle drivers

| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function        | Pathway(s)            |
|--------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------------|
| CCND1  | down      | Cyclin D1, G1/S      | Cell Cycle, Mitotic   |
| CDK2   | down      | Cyclin-dependent kinase | Cell Cycle, Mitotic   |
| BRCA1  | down      | Homologous recomb. repair | DNA Repair            |

Comparisons and Confidence  
All pathway enrichments derive from bulk RNA-seq DE (single-modality). No proteomics or phospho-data are available to cross-validate. Down-regulated DNA-repair hits may predispose to genomic instability, but require orthogonal validation (e.g., γH2AX staining).

Implications  
CBD treatment in CRC cells appears to:  
- Induce intrinsic apoptosis via BAX/CASP3 activation and BCL2 suppression  
- Enforce cell-cycle arrest at G1/S through CCND1/CDK2/E2F1 down-regulation  
- Compromise DNA repair capacity via BRCA1/RAD51/ATM down-regulation  
- Rewire MAPK and AP-1 signaling, potentially altering stress responses  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate key apoptosis and cell-cycle markers (cleaved caspase-3, cyclin D1) by Western blot or flow cytometry.  
2. Perform cell-cycle profiling (e.g., PI staining) to confirm G1/S arrest.  
3. Assess DNA-damage accumulation under CBD (γH2AX immunofluorescence).  
4. Explore dose–response of IL6 induction and its impact on tumor–stromal signaling.  

References  
None (no external PMIDs/PMCIDs retrieved via literature tools).
